Chalaadi Glacier

The most accessible glacier near Mestia — a short drive up the valley and a two-hour walk to the ice tongue.

Time needed
4 h
From Tbilisi
480 km · 8:50
Road
Mostly paved
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
June–September
Entry
free

The Chalaadi glacier flows down from the main Caucasus ridge and is the easiest glacier to reach from Mestia. That makes it the logical choice for a first full day in Svaneti: no guide, no mountaineering equipment and no dawn start are required.

The route is straightforward. From Mestia you drive north-east up the Mestiachala valley for about seven kilometres to a small parking area where the road ends. From there a path crosses the river on a suspension bridge, climbs through birch and alder forest, and then works its way up loose glacial moraine. It is roughly an hour each way, or up to three hours in total with stops and photographs.

What you will see:

  • The suspension bridge over the Mestiachala — it sways, but it is entirely safe
  • Dense riverside forest that gives way abruptly to bare glacial rubble
  • The ice tongue itself, grey-brown with debris, with meltwater caves at its base

Keep expectations realistic. Like most glaciers in the Caucasus, Chalaadi is retreating, so the ice edge sits slightly further back each year. Climbing onto the ice or entering the caves is strongly discouraged: the surface is unstable and collapses are common. From the lower moraine the view is more than enough to grasp the scale of the thing.

Practical advice

Start in the morning. Cloud usually fills the valley after midday and rain follows. Wear proper walking shoes with grip — the last section crosses loose stone and is unpleasant in trainers. Carry water and a snack, since nothing is reliably sold at the trailhead. Temperatures drop sharply at the ice, so bring a jacket even in July. The walk is manageable with children if they are comfortable on the swinging bridge. Allow about three hours from car to car and do not plan anything tight afterwards.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Tbilisi you first drive to Mestia — 470 km and eight to nine hours via Zugdidi and the Enguri gorge. From Mestia it is roughly seven to nine kilometres up the Mestiachala valley to the trailhead parking. The first part is asphalt; the last few kilometres are gravel with potholes and shallow drainage cuts. In dry weather a crossover handles it easily, while with a sedan it is better to stop a kilometre early and walk. Fill up in Mestia, as there is no fuel in the valley. Local drivers also run transfers from the town centre if you would rather not take your own car up.

Nearby places

Lake

Koruldi Lakes

Small alpine pools at 2,740 m above Mestia, facing Mount Ushba — reachable only by 4x4 or on foot.

Town

Mestia and the Svan Towers

Upper Svaneti's main town at 1,500 m — medieval stone defence towers, two strong museums and the trailhead for every route in the region.

Ski area

Hatsvali and Tetnuldi Ski Areas

Mestia's two ski zones — Hatsvali with sheltered forest runs, and Tetnuldi, where the lifts pass 3,000 metres.
